title: Adaptive Fidelity Decision Log & Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document captures the decision rationale and operational playbook for adaptive-fidelity behavior in the serving runtime. It is intended for oncall engineers, runtime operators, and product owners who must make or review changes to fidelity-orchestration policies (quality <-> cost <-> latency tradeoffs) and eviction/topology actions during normal operations and incidents.

Why this exists:
- Adaptive fidelity (also known as fidelity orchestration) is the runtime component that reduces model or execution fidelity to preserve SLOs (latency/availability) during capacity pressure or incident scenarios.
- Without a documented decision trail and safe runbook, fidelity changes risk causing silent quality regressions or customer-impacting rollbacks.

Scope and systems referenced:
- fidelity-orchestrator (service): policy engine that issues fidelity-advice (quantize, half-precision, variant-switch, reduce-beam) and hard actions (route-to-variant, throttle, shed).
- runtime-orchestrator: accepts fidelity advice and performs routing/eviction as well as kv-cache coordination.
- scheduler-gw / kernel-shepherd: component responsible for admission control and kernel selection.
- eviction-operator: cross-node component that enacts shard-level evictions and reports consistency fences.

Decision log (chronological highlights):
1) 2025-07-21 — Adopted a two-tier fidelity policy: advisory (soft) and enforced (hard). Rationale: allow safe observability and gradual rollouts. Owner: Runtimes team.
2) 2025-11-03 — Introduced "fidelity-budget" per tenant to bound economic impact during long incidents. Rationale: protect high-value tenants from repeated large-quality shifts. Owner: Finance+Runtimes.
3) 2026-01-10 — Default policy change: prefer model-variant-switch to kernel-level quantization for burst-induced latency SLO preservation. Rationale: empirical regressions in long-form generation when live-quantizing. Owner: Applied ML + Runtimes.

Operational guarantees and SLO mappings:
- Safety boundary: any enforced fidelity change must be logged and include a validated rollback path (automated or documented manual steps).
- Quality SLO: per-model baseline eval_score (internal eval harness metric). Hard guard: enforced fidelity must not reduce eval_score by > 3 percentage points without explicit stakeholder signoff.
- Latency SLOs (examples):
  - short-response 95th pctl <= 120ms (route preference: low-latency variants)
  - completion 99th pctl <= 1s for <512 tokens on dedicated pools
- Cost guardrails: fidelity-budget throttle at 30% monthly overspend triggers notification and limits further enforced fidelity changes.

Playbook: when fidelity-orchestrator recommends a change (automated or manual)
1) Triage and context (owner: oncall/runtime):
   - Confirm trigger: kernel queue length > Q_HIGH (default 4x baseline) OR node-eviction-in-flight OR NVTHERMAL alert.
   - Pull recent traces: runtime-orchestrator/traces/<request_id> and fidelity-orchestrator/decision/<decision_id>.
   - Check related KPIs: 95p latency, kernel-queue-depth, model-kvcache-hit-rate.

2) Advisory mode (first 10 minutes):
   - Apply advisory-only advice in fidelity-orchestrator (no enforced routing).
   - Create a short-lived traffic mirror (shadow) to the advised variant for perf/quality verification. Use CLI:
     rdxctl fidelity advise --tenant $TENANT --policy burst-preserve-latency --mode advisory --duration 10m
   - Observe: latency, token-cost delta, eval-score proxy (short sample prompt set).

3) Enforce-only after verification (manual or automated conditional):
   - If advisory mirror shows latency improvement >= 30% on key cohorts and eval-score proxy degradation <= 1.5 points, proceed to a staged enforce:
     a) Canary group (1% traffic) for 5 minutes
     b) Gradual ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30 minutes if KPIs healthy
   - rdxctl fidelity enforce --tenant $TENANT --policy model-variant-switch --canary 1% --rollback-window 30m

4) Rollback and emergency revert:
   - Automated rollback conditions (runtime-orchestrator): 95p latency increases by > 20% vs baseline OR error-rate spike > 5x
   - Manual rollback steps (oncall):
     1. rdxctl fidelity rollback --decision <decision_id>
     2. Validate KV-consistency: rdxctl kvcache check --shard <shard_id> and wait for fence=clear (max 2m).
     3. If kvcache fence fails, escalate to eviction-operator owners and follow "KV recovery and rehydration" runbook (link below).

Safety checklist before any enforced policy is applied:
- Owner and reviewer listed in fidelity decision record (email + ticket).
- Corresponding canary health dashboards created: latency, error-rate, cost-per-token, eval-proxy.
- Rollback automation verified and tested in the last 72h (smoke).

Runbook: emergency fidelity hard-stop (when incident requires immediate preservation of availability)
- Trigger: simultaneous NVTHERMAL + kernel-watchdog + 95p latency > SLO and burst length > 10s.
- Action (immediate):
  1) Oncall executes: rdxctl fidelity emergency-hold --global --reason "thermal+queue"
  2) runtime-orchestrator will immediately switch affected routing to pre-approved low-fidelity variants (predefined set) and disable new long-running kernels.
  3) Notify impacted tenants via incident channel and open incident ticket with tag runtime-fidelity-emergency.
  4) Begin 15-minute observation window. If stability returns, begin staged re-enable per "Playbook" above.

KV cache and eviction coordination notes:
- Eviction ordering: eviction-operator must ensure kvcache fence idempotency: eviction-operator -> runtime-orchestrator: POST /eviction/start -> include fence_id -> runtime-orchestrator acknowledges -> proceed.
- If an enforced fidelity change requires variant swap with incompatible KV layout, follow this sequence:
  1) Advisory mirror (no kvcache writes)
  2) Quiesce writes to kvcache shard: rdxctl kvcache drain --shard <id> --timeout 60s
  3) Perform variant swap and warmstart new kernels
  4) Rehydrate cache via background replay (rate-limited)

Example policy config (JSON snippet to be used in fidelity-orchestrator):
{
  "policy_id": "burst-preserve-latency-v2",
  "triggers": {
    "kernel_queue_multiplier": 3.5,
    "node_cpu_usage": 0.85
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "type": "model_variant_switch",
      "variants": ["variant-latency-1", "variant-latency-2"],
      "scope": "tenant"
    }
  ],
  "guards": {
    "max_eval_drop_pct": 3.0,
    "cost_budget_pct": 30
  }
}

Smoke tests (pre-deploy validation):
- Synthetic microburst: simulate 10s 10x traffic spike against staging clusters with fidelity-budget=unbounded and ensure auto-advisory path runs without errors.
- KV compatibility test: run variant-swap + cache-drain + rehydrate sequence in a local 3-node staging cluster. Verify no dropped requests and latency within 2x baseline.
- Canary rollback test: force an error-rate spike and verify the automated rollback completes within the configured rollback-window.

Dashboards and alerts (minimum set):
- fidelity-orchestrator/decisions (counts by type, avg latency benefit, avg eval-proxy delta)
- runtime-orchestrator/95p-latency-by-tenant (alert: > SLO*1.25 for 5m)
- kvcache/eviction-fence-failures (alert: >0 in 10m)
- scheduler-gw/kernel-queue-depth (warning: > baseline*3)

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owners: Runtimes team (oncall rotation: runtimes-oncall@redwood.com).
- Secondary owners: Applied ML (quality regressions), SRE (eviction/cluster stability), Finance (fidelity budget overrun).
- Escalation path: oncall -> service-owner -> SRE lead -> VP Eng. Use incident tag: runtime-fidelity.

Post-incident analysis and required artifacts:
- Decision record update: add reason, traces, metrics and signed-off owner within 48 hours.
- Eval-run: run the canonical eval set for affected models (mark baseline vs post-change) and store results in /evals/fidelity/<decision_id>.
- Experiment: if an enforced policy was used, create an experiment ticket to test alternate mitigations (e.g., latency-aware batching) within 14 days.

Appendix A — Quick CLI cheatsheet:
- Advise (advisory-only): rdxctl fidelity advise --tenant $TENANT --policy $POLICY --duration 10m
- Enforce with canary: rdxctl fidelity enforce --tenant $TENANT --policy $POLICY --canary 1% --rollback-window 30m
- Rollback: rdxctl fidelity rollback --decision <decision_id>
- KV drain: rdxctl kvcache drain --shard <shard_id> --timeout 60s

Appendix B — Example staging test matrix (table):
- Test | Goal | Pass criteria
- Synthetic microburst | ensure advisory path triggers | advisory decision recorded, no errors
- Variant-swap + rehydrate | KV compatibility during swap | no requests dropped, cache warm within 10m
- Canary rollback | verify rollback automation | rollback completes within 2x rollback-window
